transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, I really don't want to waste your time with anything too silly. But, well, I guess what brings me in is... I've been noticing I kind of, you know, plan my days around not having to drive over those really high bridges. 

It's just a little quirk, honestly, nothing too crazy. And, I mean, if I absolutely can't get around it, I'll do it... I just sort of white-knuckle the steering wheel the whole way across until I'm back on solid ground. Is that... does that make sense? I hope that's the sort of thing you handle here.
When you avoid high bridges, is it specifically when you're driving, or does this happen in other situations too, like walking across a high bridge or even just thinking about being on one?

Well, um... it's mostly just when I'm in the car. Thinking about it isn't too bad, really. I don't want to make it sound like some huge issue. 

I mean, I know those bridges over the bay are built perfectly fine, and folks drive over them every single day without a second thought. But... well, when I actually get near one, it's just this silly feeling. My mind kind of plays tricks on me and acts like the car could just go right over the side. 

I know that probably sounds a bit foolish for a guy my age, right? I hope I'm explaining it okay. It's really just a weird little thought that pops up when I'm at the wheel.
When you feel this fear while driving over high bridges, does it ever happen in other driving situations, like tunnels or highways, or is it limited only to high bridges?

No, no, it's really just the high bridges. Tunnels and highways are completely fine. I mean, I drive on the highway to work every day, no problem at all. It's just... I guess it's just that specific height over the water that gets to me a little bit. 

I'm not trying to be difficult or anything, it's just that one very specific thing. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing. It's just... well, just the bridges.

latest_inference.note: The patient's fear is specifically limited to driving over high bridges, which aligns with situational type specific phobia. No other phobic disorders are indicated based on the dialogue.
